cell: completes set work with encouragement and guidance (Studies and sets goals because they are asked to; sees success as marks and ability as largely given.)
practice: completes set work when encouraged and sets goals because a tutor asks for them
knows: what the task asks and what marks mean, with success read as the grade
self_identity: a learner who sees ability as fixed and success as marks

cell: completes set tasks to given criteria with guidance (Studies and reads feedback because it is required; sees assessment as tests to pass and feedback as the mark.)
practice: does set tasks to the criteria given and reads the mark and comments because they must
knows: what the criteria for a task ask, with feedback read as the mark
self_identity: a learner who sees assessment as tests to pass

cell: finds information for a set task from sources a tutor names (Searches because the task asks for sources; takes the first results that look relevant.)
practice: looks in the books and sites a tutor lists and uses whatever first seems to fit
knows: the facts a task needs and where the named sources keep them
self_identity: a learner who searches only when a task demands sources

cell: acknowledges sources in a set format with guidance (Acknowledges sources because the rules say so; sees referencing as avoiding trouble.)
practice: acknowledges sources in a set referencing format with guidance because the rules require it
knows: the set format and the rule that sources must be named
self_identity: a learner who sees referencing as a way to avoid trouble

cell: questions a source when prompted (Questions a source when asked to; sees being critical as finding fault.)
practice: questions a source when a tutor asks and looks for what is wrong with it
knows: what a source says and the questions a task asks of it
self_identity: a learner who sees being critical as finding fault

cell: writes a short assignment to a set structure with guidance (Writes because the assignment requires it, to a structure they are given.)
practice: writes a short assignment to the structure given, following guidance step by step
knows: the structure set for a task and the facts and ideas it needs
self_identity: a learner who writes because the assignment requires it

cell: presents set material clearly with guidance (Presents and joins groups because it is assessed; aims to get through it.)
practice: presents set material clearly with guidance, aiming to get through the assessed talk
knows: the content set and the basic steps of giving a talk
self_identity: a learner who presents because it is assessed

cell: revises set material and sits exams with guidance (Revises because the exam is coming; reads and rereads, and aims to get through.)
practice: reads and rereads the set notes before an exam and sits the paper as the tutor directs
knows: the facts and topics the exam is likely to cover, as given in class
self_identity: a learner who revises because the exam is coming and aims to get through

cell: completes a small, well-defined investigation set by a tutor (prescribed research) (Investigates because the task requires it; sees research as following steps to an answer someone else expects.)
practice: follows a tutor's set steps to carry out a small investigation and reports the answer found
knows: the steps of a set investigation and the facts it needs
self_identity: a learner who treats research as steps towards an answer someone else already holds

cell: completes a short reflection on a well-defined task with guidance (Reflects because the task asks for it; sees reflection as something to complete, and is not yet aware of how they learn.)
practice: writes a short reflection on a set task using the prompts a tutor gives
knows: what happened in the task and what the reflection prompts ask for
self_identity: a learner who reflects when told to, without yet seeing how they learn

cell: completes well-defined tasks in a setting under close supervision (Takes part because the course requires it; sees the placement as tasks to get through.)
practice: completes the tasks set on placement under close supervision and does what the supervisor asks
knows: what the tasks in a setting involve and the rules to follow there
self_identity: a learner who sees a placement as tasks to get through

cell: uses AI tools within stated rules with guidance (Uses or avoids AI because the rules say so; follows instructions on it.)
practice: uses or avoids AI tools as the rules say, following the tutor's instructions
knows: the stated rules on AI use for a task
self_identity: a learner who treats AI use as a matter of following rules

cell: generates ideas when prompted (Generates ideas when a task asks for them; prefers a known answer.)
practice: jots down a few ideas when a task asks and settles fast on the answer that feels safe
knows: the ideas and facts a task calls for
self_identity: a learner who prefers a right answer to a new one

cell: describes themselves as a learner, what they are good at and want from study, when prompted (Tells their story when asked; sees identity as given, not made. Affective domain: receiving.)
practice: describes self as a learner when asked and keeps to the tasks set
knows: what they are good at and want from study, in their own words
self_identity: a learner who sees identity as given rather than made

cell: Explain what excelling at university means

cell: Understand how learning works in a discipline's discourse community

self_identity: a newcomer who sees learning as joining a community's conversation

cell: Explain how academic searching differs from everyday searching

cell: Explain why academic work acknowledges its sources

practice: maps who has written on a topic and where they agree or differ, then asks what each voice adds to the debate

self_identity: a newcomer who sees scholarship as a conversation one can question

cell: Interpret an assessment question's steer and keywords before writing
practice: reads an assessment question for its steer and keywords, marking the task words and limits before writing anything

cell: Explain what a presentation tests and read its brief
practice: reads a presentation brief for its time, format and audience and explains what the task tests

self_identity: a newcomer who sees presenting as a practice worth learning

cell: Explain the forms of exam and what each demands
practice: names the exam forms a module sets, such as essay, multiple-choice, open-book and short-answer, and says what each asks for

knows: what a research project is, how it differs from an essay and how a proposal plans it
self_identity: a newcomer who sees research as a practice distinct from essay writing

cell: Apply the describe, reflect, take action cycle
practice: writes a reflection in three steps, describing an event, reflecting on its meaning and naming an action to take
knows: what reflective practice is and how the describe, reflect, take action cycle works
self_identity: a newcomer who sees reflection as a practice with its own method

cell: Distinguish the types of practice- and work-based learning
practice: sorts examples of placements, internships, work experience and practice learning into their types and names each one
knows: the types of practice-based and work-based learning and how they differ
self_identity: a newcomer who sees that learning happens at work as well as in class

cell: Explain what generative AI is and is not
practice: explains in plain terms how a generative AI tool predicts text and what it does not do, such as know or understand
knows: what generative AI is, how it works at a high level and what it is not
self_identity: a newcomer who sees AI as a tool with limits

cell: Recognise creativity as a developable skill, related to critical thinking
practice: names creative moves in others' work and shows how creativity links to critical thinking
knows: what creativity is, that it can be developed and how it relates to critical thinking
self_identity: a newcomer who sees creativity as something to learn, not a gift

knows: what academic practice, an academic practitioner and graduate identity are

follows the writing cycle from analysing the task and planning through to a completed first draft, with support

a student trying out writing as a process rather than a single sitting

self_identity:
a student trying out presenting by a set method

cell: Make a simple revision plan from the time available

a student trying out revision as something planned rather than left to the last week

how a research question, rationale and aims fit together and what makes each clear

a student trying out the work of a researcher for the first time

cell: Balance positives and negatives
practice:
records what went well alongside what went badly in a reflective entry and gives each its due weight

self_identity:
a student trying reflection as a fair account rather than praise or blame

cell: Explain what learning in practice offers
practice: explains how a placement or practice task puts classroom theory to use and what that authentic learning adds to study
knows:
how practice-based learning works as authentic learning in which theory meets practice

a student who sees practice as a place to learn

self_identity:
a student trying to use AI within the rules

cell: Keep a record of own learning, strengths and goals

a student who keeps account of their own learning

cell: Adopt a growth mindset towards academic challenge

own critical habits and gaps and where critical choices already happen in study

a student beginning to see themself as a critical thinker all the time, not only for marks

what makes a question researchable and the limits of own time, access and skill

FHEQ 4.18.b1: defines a new claim against the scholarly record by showing what it builds on, departs from and adds, so others can trace and test it. Evidenced as a thesis bibliography in law, citation of datasets in biosciences and an annotated relation to prior work in philosophy.
self_identity:
a researcher whose record others can trust and who holds colleagues to the same standard

cell: acts as a critical being in knowledge, the self and the world: transformatory critique (Critical being is a mode of doing and expression, fluent and in the flow; critique becomes transformatory, communicated to make new knowledge in the service of their disciplinary community.)
practice:
builds a thesis argument that challenges a field's assumptions, defends it in a viva and carries the critique into policy, practice or public debate

FHEQ 4.18.b5: defends the critique in a viva and carries it into policy, practice or public debate, judging soundly on incomplete evidence and explaining it to experts and the public. Evidenced as a viva defence in history, a policy submission in public health and a public lecture in environmental science.
knows:
critique as the making of knowledge: questioning a field's assumptions and categories so that new knowledge can be proposed, debated and refined at the edge of understanding

FHEQ 4.18.b1: makes new knowledge by critique, reframing a problem so that the field can see and argue it differently. Evidenced as a theoretical intervention in sociology, a reinterpretation of sources in history and a critique of a standard model in economics.

FHEQ 4.18.b2: commands the critical traditions of own field at its forefront, knowing what each leaves unexamined and where critique can open new knowledge. Evidenced as a thesis literature chapter in philosophy, a field review article in education and a theoretical critique in law.
self_identity:
a critical being whose questioning changes how others in the field and beyond understand a problem

FHEQ 4.18.b6: becomes a researcher whose ongoing critical work adds new ideas and approaches that change how others in the field frame a problem. Evidenced as a programme of published research in sociology, a new clinical guideline in nursing and a funded research project in engineering.

FHEQ 4.18.b7: becomes a critical being who takes responsibility for questioning in complex and unpredictable settings, leading change in the field and beyond with largely autonomous initiative. cell: communicates original research to specialist and non-specialist audiences (Writing is a mode of doing and expression, fluent and in the flow; they communicate original knowledge in the discipline's forms in the service of their disciplinary community.)
practice:
writes a thesis, journal articles, a grant proposal and a plain-language summary from the same research, revising each in answer to reviewers and editors

FHEQ 4.18.b1: writes a thesis and journal articles from original research and revises them in answer to reviewers until the work is fit to publish and extends the field. Evidenced as a doctoral thesis in history, a peer-reviewed article in biomedical science and a monograph chapter in philosophy.

FHEQ 4.18.b5: writes a grant proposal and a plain-language summary from the same research, judging what each specialist or lay reader needs and stating conclusions clearly. Evidenced as a funding bid in engineering, a lay summary in health research and a policy briefing in social science.
knows:
writing understood as the medium in which knowledge is defined: through language one proposes new knowledge at a discipline's boundaries, debates and refines it and adds to a living discourse

FHEQ 4.18.b1: defines new knowledge in language: the written argument is where the claim is made, bounded, qualified and offered to the discipline's debate. Evidenced as a doctoral thesis in English, a journal article in physics and a book chapter in anthropology.
self_identity:
a scholarly author whose writing is published, reviewed and used by others

FHEQ 4.18.b6: becomes a scholarly author whose continuing writing adds new ideas and approaches that others read, cite and build on. Evidenced as a publication record in sociology, a cited methods paper in psychology and an edited collection in history.

FHEQ 4.18.b7: becomes an author who takes responsibility for own published work and handles review, editing and public reaction with largely autonomous judgement. Evidenced as a response to reviewers in medicine, an editorial role record in education and a commissioned report in public policy.

cell: disseminates original research and leads collaboration in the research community (Presenting and collaborating are fluent and tacit, a mode of doing and expression in the flow; they communicate and test knowledge in the service of their disciplinary community.)
practice:
defends a thesis in a viva, gives conference papers and invited talks, chairs sessions, teaches and explains research to policymakers and the public

FHEQ 4.18.b5: defends a thesis in a viva, gives conference papers and explains research to policymakers and the public, judging complex issues soundly when evidence is incomplete. knows:
speaking as a medium of knowledge-making: the conference, the viva and the public talk as where new claims are proposed, tested under questioning and refined

FHEQ 4.18.b1: puts new knowledge into the field's conversation aloud, where questions test it and refine it before and after it is written. Evidenced as a conference paper in linguistics, a viva in engineering and a research seminar in politics.
self_identity:
a researcher whose spoken voice carries the work into the field and beyond

FHEQ 4.18.b6: becomes a researcher whose talks and teaching carry continuing research into the field, spreading new ideas and approaches others take up. Evidenced as an invited keynote in education, a teaching portfolio in biology and a recorded research seminar series in history.

FHEQ 4.18.b7: becomes a leader who chairs sessions and leads collaboration with largely autonomous initiative, taking responsibility in complex and unpredictable research settings. Evidenced as a conference chairing record in psychology, a research network leadership role in engineering and a policy advisory briefing in public health.

cell: holds a field in command for oral examination and examines others (Command of the field is fluent and tacit, a mode of doing and expression in the flow; they examine and are examined in the service of their disciplinary community.)
practice:
prepares for a viva by rehearsing the whole thesis and its field under questioning, then examines others' theses and sets and moderates assessment

FHEQ 4.18.b5: rehearses the whole thesis under questioning before a viva, then examines others' theses and moderates assessment, judging complex work soundly and explaining decisions clearly. Evidenced as a mock viva in history, an external examiner report in nursing and a moderation record in engineering.
knows:
a field held in command well enough to define what is new in own work and defend it under examination at the boundary of current understanding

FHEQ 4.18.b1: knows the field well enough to state precisely what one's own work adds, and to hold that line under questioning. Evidenced as a viva defence in physics, an oral examination in medicine and a doctoral defence in music.

FHEQ 4.18.b2: holds a substantial body of forefront knowledge in command, recalling its debates, methods and literature fluently when questioned. Evidenced as a viva defence in sociology, a qualifying examination in physics and an oral examination in philosophy.
self_identity:
an examiner and examinee who holds a field well enough to judge others' command of it

FHEQ 4.18.b7: becomes an examiner and examinee trusted with the responsibility of judging others' command of a field, acting with largely autonomous judgement. Evidenced as an external examiner role in law, a doctoral examination panel record in biology and an assessment board contribution in education.

cell: creates original research of a quality to satisfy peer review; acts as an independent researcher across knowledge, personal effectiveness, research governance and engagement (Research is a mode of doing and expression: questions, methods and writing come fluently, in the flow; they make and communicate original knowledge in the service of their disciplinary community, as an expression of their commitment to it.)
practice:
designs original studies, secures ethical approval and funding, publishes through peer review, manages data and engagement and supervises others' research

FHEQ 4.18.b1: produces original findings that pass peer review and move the field forward, writing them up for the disciplinary community. Evidenced as a refereed article in chemistry, a doctoral thesis in history and a peer-reviewed practice output in design.

FHEQ 4.18.b3: conceives and runs original studies with ethical approval and funding, redesigning them when unexpected problems arise in the field. Evidenced as a funded project in public health, a revised trial protocol in medicine and an adapted fieldwork design in anthropology.

FHEQ 4.18.b6: keeps contributing new methods and ideas through a sustained research programme and supervises others' research within it. Evidenced as a new analytic technique in computing, a methods paper in sociology and a supervised doctoral cohort in education.
knows:
research method as how knowledge is defined: designing enquiries that generate new knowledge at the forefront and justifying why their findings count as knowledge

FHEQ 4.18.b1: designs and carries out enquiry that produces new knowledge good enough for peer review and argues why its methods make it knowledge. Evidenced as an experimental thesis in biology, an ethnography in anthropology and a mixed-methods study in public health.

FHEQ 4.18.b6: develops new techniques or approaches to enquiry that others in the field can take up. Evidenced as a new analytical method in statistics, a methodological paper in education and an instrument validated in psychology.

FHEQ 4.18.b4: commands the frontier methodologies of own field in detail, along with the governance and data rules that frame them. Evidenced as a methods chapter in a psychology thesis, a data governance plan in health research and a methodological review in linguistics.

FHEQ 4.18.b2: holds a systematic grasp of the forefront of the field and of how funding and engagement carry new knowledge to its users. Evidenced as a grant application in engineering, an impact case study in social policy and a review article in biology.
self_identity:
an independent researcher accountable for the knowledge they make and the people they train

FHEQ 4.18.b7: acts as an independent researcher answerable for the knowledge made and for the people trained, in settings that no rule fully settles. Evidenced as a principal investigator role in physics, a doctoral supervision record in nursing and a research ethics committee seat in law.

cell: uses reflexivity as part of research method, so that the account of the knowledge made includes the maker; manages own development and career as a researcher (Reflection has become a mode of doing and expression, fluent and largely tacit, like an athlete in the flow; reflexivity is how they make and communicate knowledge in the service of their disciplinary community, and an expression of their commitment to it.)
practice:
builds reflexivity into research method through a positionality statement, a reflexive log and analysis that shows the researcher's part, then teaches reflective practice to others

FHEQ 4.18.b1: builds reflexivity into research method so that published original knowledge includes an account of the researcher's own part in making it. Evidenced as a refereed qualitative article in sociology, a doctoral thesis in education and an autoethnography in performing arts.

FHEQ 4.18.b5: judges how own presence shaped complex findings and explains that clearly to peers and to students learning reflective practice. Evidenced as a reflexive methods paper in nursing, a conference keynote in anthropology and a postgraduate workshop in social work.
knows:
reflexivity as part of how knowledge is defined: showing how the knower's position shapes the new knowledge proposed, so that the claim and its making are judged together

FHEQ 4.18.b1: builds the researcher's part into the account of what is found, so the new knowledge carries a clear statement of how it was made. Evidenced as a reflexive methods chapter in social work, an autoethnography in education and a practitioner-researcher account in nursing.

FHEQ 4.18.b4: understands in detail the reflexive methodologies of own field and how a researcher's presence is accounted for in method and writing. Evidenced as a methodology chapter in health research, a methods review in geography and a reflexive framework paper in education.
self_identity:
a researcher who makes their own part in the knowledge visible and teaches others to do the same

FHEQ 4.18.b7: becomes a researcher who makes own part in knowledge visible, manages own career and teaches others the same practice with full independence. Evidenced as a doctoral supervision record in psychology, a research career plan in nursing and a reflective practice module led in teacher education.

cell: makes original knowledge from and for practice, as a researcher and a practitioner at once (Practice is a mode of doing and expression, fluent and in the flow; they research and change it, communicating what they learn in the service of their professional and disciplinary community.)
practice:
carries out practitioner research or a professional doctorate in own workplace, changes practice from the findings and shares them with professional bodies and journals

FHEQ 4.18.b6: carries out practitioner research in own workplace that develops new techniques and approaches and changes how the work is done. Evidenced as an action research project in education, a quality improvement study in nursing and a practice innovation in engineering.

FHEQ 4.18.b1: produces original knowledge from practice that passes peer review and is published in professional and academic journals. Evidenced as a professional doctorate thesis in social work, a refereed article in health care and a practice-led publication in design.

FHEQ 4.18.b5: makes informed judgements on complex practice problems and communicates findings clearly to practitioners, professional bodies and researchers. Evidenced as a professional body briefing in pharmacy, a conference paper in education and a policy report in public health.
knows:
practice as a source of new knowledge: defining knowledge from and for professional practice so that what practice finds enters both the profession's and the academy's discourse

FHEQ 4.18.b1: turns findings from practice into knowledge the field can test and use, written for both practitioners and scholars. Evidenced as an action research thesis in education, a professional doctorate in nursing and a practice evaluation in social work.

FHEQ 4.18.b2: holds a systematic grasp of professional knowledge at the forefront of own field and how research and practice inform each other. Evidenced as a doctoral literature review in nursing, a practice framework in business and a state of the field paper in social work.

FHEQ 4.18.b4: understands in detail practice-based and action research methods and when each suits enquiry in own workplace. Evidenced as a methodology chapter in education, a research design for a clinical audit and an action research protocol in management.
self_identity:
a researcher-practitioner trusted in both the profession and the academy

FHEQ 4.18.b7: becomes a researcher-practitioner trusted in both profession and academy, acting with autonomy and responsibility in complex practice. Evidenced as a consultant practitioner role in nursing, a professional doctorate in education and a research lead post in engineering.

cell: shapes responsible AI practice in the research community (Responsible AI use is fluent and tacit, a mode of doing and expression in the flow, in the service of their disciplinary community.)
practice:
uses and discloses AI in research to the field's standards, writes it into data management and ethics plans and helps set a research group's or department's AI policy

FHEQ 4.18.b5: the researcher judges complex questions of AI in research, writes them into data management and ethics plans and explains the case to colleagues and policy makers. Evidenced as a research ethics application in psychology, a departmental AI policy in engineering and a methods paper in digital humanities.
knows:
AI as a new medium in knowledge-making: how it changes the way knowledge is produced, checked and attributed, with own part in defining responsible norms for it

FHEQ 4.18.b1: makes and reports new knowledge with AI in the method while showing how its use shapes what counts as reliable and attributable. Evidenced as an AI-assisted analysis in linguistics, a computational study in bioinformatics and a disclosure of AI use in a law thesis.

FHEQ 4.18.b2: the researcher holds a systematic grasp of AI's methodological, ethical and legal implications for research and publishing at the forefront of their own field. Evidenced as a thesis chapter on research ethics in sociology, a journal article in bioinformatics and a doctoral review in law.

FHEQ 4.18.b4: the researcher understands in detail how AI changes the techniques of enquiry their field relies on, from data handling to analysis and peer review. Evidenced as a methods chapter in computational linguistics, a data management plan in genomics and a viva defence in education.
self_identity:
a researcher who helps a field decide how AI should and should not be used

FHEQ 4.18.b7: the researcher becomes a voice who helps the field decide how AI should and should not be used, acting autonomously in fast-changing professional settings. cell: creates new knowledge and opens new directions in a field (Creative thinking is fluent and tacit, a mode of doing and expression in the flow, in the service of their disciplinary community.)

opens new lines of enquiry in a thesis, turns findings into new methods, products or ventures and leads innovation with partners beyond the university

knows:
creativity as the origin of new knowledge: ideas generated at a field's boundaries that, once tested and argued, redefine what the field knows and can do

FHEQ 4.18.b6: creates new techniques, ideas or approaches that change how the field works, not only what it knows. Evidenced as a new compositional technique in music, a prototype method in engineering and a new genre of practice in performance.

FHEQ 4.18.b2: the researcher holds a systematic grasp of their field's frontier, knowing where it is stuck and how original research becomes innovation in practice. Evidenced as a thesis literature review in chemistry, a research agenda paper in education and a state-of-the-art review in computing.
self_identity:
an innovator who shapes the field's creative practice and others' identity as creators

FHEQ 4.18.b7: the researcher becomes an innovator who shapes the field's creative practice and helps others see themselves as creators, acting autonomously in unpredictable settings. cell: authors their own scholarly identity, examining their own and their field's assumptions, and advances the practice of their community (Identity and values are lived without prompting, a practitioner who authors themselves and their field. Affective domain: characterisation by a value system.)

argues own standpoint in a thesis and its viva, mentors students and early-career colleagues through questions of identity and values and models a scholarly self in teaching and public work

FHEQ 4.18.b5: the researcher argues their own standpoint in a thesis and viva, mentors others through questions of identity and values and models a scholarly self in teaching and public work. Evidenced as a viva defence in sociology, a mentoring record in education and a public lecture in history.
knows:
the scholarly self as a source of knowledge: how one's standpoint, argued in a thesis and a viva, shapes and defines the new knowledge one proposes

self_identity:
a scholar who has authored a professional self, holds it open to question and helps others author theirs
